chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Red Allen's New Orleans delivery and his years with Armstrong
summary: Butler recalls Red Allen's rise with Louis Russell at the Saratoga Club and his soulful solo on You Gave Me Everything But Love, and says he stayed with Armstrong to learn and save his lip.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Oh, I know what I wanted to ask you about, too, since we're talking about that period, players, Red Allen?
My man! /Now, Red Allen came up there with -- I think his band was called (inaudible). That was a New Orleans band. And I think he played with --

Yes. Louis Russell. And they had a band, they played in the Saratoga Club. So that's when Red became famous. And Red played a solo on the thing called, "You Gave Me Everything But Love." And he played, I think it was the Apollo -- I think it was the other theater, I forget the name but I'll get it in a few minutes, and he played a solo on that. And the solo was so soulful that he became famous for that.
And Red Allen had that thing, that same New Orleans or Louisiana delivery, And it would remind you of Louis Armstrong, because he'd do the same thing effect.
But he also had some -- but the intervals
that he was playing, he was doing --
The approach, see. He never had that approach. And so automatically he -- that was it.
Do you have any idea why he stayed with Armstrong's band so long?
Because he was learning. And then he was saving Armstrong.

Yes. / And he was learning. You stay there and learn, and my goodness, it was financially, economically a good idea, too. If you want to buy those homes and things, you stay there. (Inaudible) when you were in with the big stuff? Doesn't make sense.
